sentences.text: Pseudopetalichthys problematica was a lightly armored placoderm, an ancient armored fish.
The single known specimen measured a total length of 15 cm.
This animal superficially resembles the genus Stensioella.
However, it differs from Stensioella in the structure of its mouth, the placement of its gill rakers, and possesses known orbits unlike Stensioella.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was originally housed in the Schlosspark Museum in Bad Kreuznach before being lost at an unknown date.
The genus Pseudopetalichthys was named by Moy-Thomas in 1939.
The only known species in the genus is Pseudopetalichthys problematica.
Parapetalichthys is a synonym for Pseudopetalichthys.
Fossils of Pseudopetalichthys have been found in the Early Devonian Hunsrückschiefer Lagerstätte in Germany.
Pseudopetalichthys lived during the Emsian stage, between 410.62 and 399.5 million years ago.
Some experts hypothesize that Pseudopetalichthys problematica and Paraplesiobatis are the same species, but this remains untestable without more fossils.
